findings.evidence: `PwC1ImmersionOn.lean:193` and `:204` define `exists_Icc_piece_right/left`, returning one-sided `ContDiffOn` pieces, while `OnCurve.lean:462-475`, `:480-493`, and `:506-519` separately demand `DifferentiableOn` inside `hγ_lip`.
findings.fix: Require only existential one-sided Lipschitz windows in all three public signatures; intersect them with the intervals from `h_imm.exists_Icc_piece_right/left`, restrict Lipschitzness, and derive the needed `DifferentiableOn` facts from those `ContDiffOn` pieces.
findings.issue: The `hγ_lip` signatures of this theorem and the declarations at lines 480 and 506 redundantly require `DifferentiableOn` on both Lipschitz windows; `h_imm` already provides breakpoint-free `C¹` intervals on both sides of every interior crossing.

summary: The three public on-curve APIs require crossing-side differentiability that already follows locally from the immersion hypothesis, making their regularity assumption unnecessarily strong.
